subject: Mutual action plan: FinApex RTBF runbook & residency risks
summary: Post-demo MAP proposal and clarifying backup/snapshot constraints, KMS considerations, and timeline for logical vs permanent deletion.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul@finapex.com>
Cc: security@finapex.com, legal@finapex.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: proposed MAP and runbook for FinApex RTBF

Hi Paul — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) so we’re aligned on what RTBF (right to be forgotten) will look like operationally for FinApex. Please review and flag anything missing.

Objective: ensure requested user records and associated artifacts are logically deleted and, where feasible, permanently unrecoverable within agreed windows while preserving compliance evidence for audits.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Formal request: FinApex submits RTBF requests via our portal (link below) or via signed request email.
2) Acknowledgement: Redwood confirms receipt within 1 business day.
3) Logical delete: Redwood marks records as deleted and removes from active indexes within 3 business days.
4) Cache/KV purge: KV caches and runtime caches cleared within 5 business days of request.
5) Backups & snapshots: backups are on a provider snapshot cadence; we can guarantee deletion from active stores but cannot always guarantee instant wipe from immutable snapshots — typical overwrite window up to 30 days.
6) Attestation: When deletion completes, Redwood provides a certificate-of-completion and a backup purge status report.

Notes/risks we discussed that need confirmation from FinApex:
- Do you require deletion to be keyed to customer-managed KMS keys? If so, rotating or revoking the keys is one mitigation to prevent restore; however, customer KMS integration affects how we provide attestation and evidence.
- Are there contractual audit log retention minimums for FinApex that would override our normal retention (we default to 90 days for request-level logs for troubleshooting unless otherwise agreed)?
- Residency: confirm whether the dataset in scope must remain in the EU region (if so we’ll route deletion workflow through our EU private controls).

Attachments: redwood-rtbf-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook outline), soc2-typeii-summary.pdf (security posture summary).

Next steps: please confirm (1) the list of user IDs/collections you want included, (2) who your security point-of-contact is for evidence acceptance, and (3) whether you want us to use customer-managed keys for this project.

Portal to submit formal request: https://portal.redwood.ai/rtbf/submit
HubSpot (internal record): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that MAP looks reasonable. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Backups/snapshots: can you confirm whether backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys today, or if they are encrypted with provider keys? If we can have CMK applied, we can rotate/revoke to make restores infeasible.

2) How quickly can you provide evidence that a user record is gone from all indexes and KV caches? We need a technical attestation for our compliance team.

3) For legal, we’ll want a Docusign-ready attestation template that confirms deletion and lists any outstanding snapshot windows. Can you attach a sample?

I’m looping in our security mailbox — they’ll respond with the ID list shortly.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Folks — adding a security runbook response and some concrete SLA numbers that we can put into the MAP. High level answers to Paul’s questions below, plus an attachment with the runbook and an example attestation (redwood-rtbf-runbook-v1.pdf).

Encryption & backups:
- Backups are encrypted at rest. Default configuration uses provider-managed keys, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for customers on Dedicated/Private plans or as part of an enterprise arrangement. If FinApex requires CMK for backups, we should add that to the MAP as a dependency and timeline item.
- If CMK is used, rotating/revoking the key is a valid mechanism to render snapshot restores infeasible; we will provide guidance on key-handback and attestation wording.

Timelines & evidence:
- Logical deletion from active indexes: target 72 hours after request (3 business days).
- KV/cache purge: target 5 business days (some caches may be sharded; we’ll include a shard-level checklist).
- Backup/snapshot window: our platform cannot always force immediate wipe of provider immutable snapshots. Typical overwrite/retention window is 30 days from snapshot creation; in rare cases provider snapshots may have longer retention (we’ll surface specifics in the evidence report).
- Audit logs: standard retention 90 days; we can negotiate extended retention if required for regulatory reasons but that will be a contract-level exception.

Attestation & deliverables:
- We’ll produce: deletion manifest (list of IDs processed), cache purge log, backup snapshot manifest (showing snapshot IDs and retention dates), and a signed attestation document.
- Example attestation will be prepared as a DocuSign template.

Action items for the MAP (security):
A) FinApex to confirm CMK requirement and provide KMS details if applicable.
B) FinApex to export and share the list of user IDs/collections to be removed (we can accept CSV attachment).
C) Redwood to accept formal RTBF request and issue acknowledgement within 1 business day.
D) Redwood to schedule deletion job and share expected date ranges for backup overwrite.

Attaching: redwood-rtbf-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook + attestation template), soc2-typeii-summary.pdf

Ben
